response.text:
{"criterion": "A mechanism is described in the filings and the outcome tests are inconclusive on the bundle's periods.", "why": "STEP 1 — MECHANISMS.

intangible_assets — PRESENT (described, unquantified as a barrier). FACT [1] (mu-20250529, Overview): "Micron delivers a rich portfolio of high-performance DRAM, NAND, and NOR memory and storage products through our Micron® and Crucial® brands." FACT [2] (mu-20250529, Intangible Assets note): "Product and process technology | $624 | $(209) | $415". FACT [3] (mu-20250529, Contingencies): "a jury rendered a verdict that Micron's memory modules infringe two asserted patents … and found that Micron should pay $425 million for infringement of the '912 patent and $20 million for infringement of the '417 patent." FACT [4] (mu-20250529, Other Operating (Income) Expense, Net): "Patent license charges | $57 | $— | $57 | $—". FACT [5] (mu-20250529, Contingencies): "The above lawsuits pertain to substantially all of our DRAM, NAND, and other memory and storage products we manufacture, which account for substantially all of our revenue." INFERENCE [6, from 1–5]: the filing evidences owned brands and capitalised process technology, but it also evidences that the company is a net payer/defendant on third-party IP across substantially all of its revenue, so the intangible stack is not shown in this bundle to be exclusionary against rivals.

switching_costs — INSUFFICIENT_EVIDENCE, and the one direct contract disclosure points the other way. FACT [7] (mu-20250529, Revenue and Customer Contract Liabilities): "Substantially all contracts with our customers are short-term in duration at fixed, negotiated prices with payment generally due shortly after delivery." FACT [8] (same note): "As of May 29, 2025, our future performance obligations beyond one year were $143 million, which included customer prepayments and other contract liabilities." FACT [9] (mu-20250529, Risk Factors): "The process to develop new products requires us to demonstrate advanced functionality, performance, and reliability, often well in advance of a planned ramp of production, in order to secure design wins with our customers." FACT [10] (mu-20250529, Risk Factors): "Developing and manufacturing system-level products with specifications unique to a customer increases our reliance upon that customer". INFERENCE [11, from 7–10]: qualification and design-win cycles are described as a cost borne by Micron to win sockets, not as a disclosed cost borne by customers to leave; no retention, renewal or churn metric appears in the bundle.

network_effects — ABSENT. FACT [12]: the bundle contains no statement that additional users increase product value to existing users; the closest demand language is FACT [13] (mu-20250529, Industry Conditions): "we experienced substantial improvements in revenue, pricing, and margins as compared to 2023, reflecting demand growth, driven in part by deployment of AI".

cost_advantage — PRESENT as a claim, NOT MEASURED against rivals. FACT [14] (mu-20250529, Overview): "We make significant investments to develop proprietary product and process technology, which generally increases bit density per wafer and reduces per-bit manufacturing costs of each generation of product." FACT [15] (mu-20250529, Consolidated Gross Margin): "DRAM margins improved primarily due to an increased mix of HBM and manufacturing cost reductions driven by improvements in product and process technology." FACT [16] (mu-20250529, Risk Factors): "A significant portion of our manufacturing costs are fixed and do not vary proportionally with changes in production output." FACT [17] (mu-20250529, Liquidity): "We estimate capital expenditures in 2025 for property, plant, and equipment, net of proceeds from government incentives, to be approximately $14 billion." INFERENCE [18, from 14–17]: cost reduction is asserted and is consistent with the disclosed gross-margin path, but the bundle contains no peer cost-per-bit or peer margin figure, so a *relative* cost advantage is unchecked.

efficient_scale — INSUFFICIENT_EVIDENCE, and the capacity evidence supplied is explicitly unquantified. FACT [19] (E-13, cx.capacity, Kioxia K2): unit field reads "no quantified capacity units given (facility described only)", quote: "a wafer fabrication facility in Kitakami, Japan, referred to as 'K2'". FACT [20] (E-13, cx.capacity, Samsung): "• Ramp up enhanced HBM3E 12H to meet initial demand", unit "no quantified capacity units given". FACT [21] (E-13, cx.capacity, SK hynix): status not_found — "Searched the full SK hynix 1Q25 press release: it states capex discipline and a demand view (HBM demand approximately doubling), but announces no capacity addition, fab or volume." FACT [22] (mu-20250529, Risk Factors): "We, and some of our competitors, have plans to ramp, or are constructing or ramping, production at new fabrication facilities. Increases in worldwide supply of semiconductor memory and storage, if not accompanied by commensurate increases in demand, could lead to declines in average selling prices for our products". INFERENCE [23, from 19–22]: the bundle shows incumbents and Micron adding capacity with no quantity attached to any of it, which is the opposite of the showing efficient scale requires.

STEP 2 — OUTCOME TESTS.

(a) Share stability: NOT SHOWN. FACT [24] (mu-20250529, Liquidity): "We expect these new fabs to be key to meeting our requirements for additional wafer capacity, in line with industry demand trends and our objective of maintaining stable bit share." FACT [25] (mu-20250529, Certain Concentrations): "Data center and networking 55% | 30%" and "Mobile 15% | 25%" of total revenue for the nine months ended May 29, 2025 and May 30, 2024. FACT [26] (mu-20250529, Risk Factors): "the CAC determined that critical information infrastructure operators in China may not purchase Micron products, impacting our revenue with companies headquartered in mainland China and Hong Kong, including direct sales as well as indirect sales through distributors." FACT [27] (mu-20250529, Risk Factors): "We face intense competition in the semiconductor memory and storage markets from a number of companies, including Kioxia Holdings Corporation; Samsung Electronics Co., Ltd.; SK hynix Inc.; Sandisk Corporation; Yangtze Memory Technologies Co., Ltd. ('YMTC'); and ChangXin Memory Technologies, Inc. ('CXMT')." INFERENCE [28, from 24–27]: stable bit share is stated as an objective, not as an achieved measurement; the percentages in [25] are Micron's own end-market mix, not share of any market, and [26] is a disclosed loss of access in one geography — so the share test cannot be resolved either way on these periods.

(b) Returns above cost of capital: NOT TESTABLE IN THIS BUNDLE. INSUFFICIENT_EVIDENCE — needed: a pre-computed return-on-invested-capital series and a cost-of-capital figure. why: the bundle contains no <computed_metrics> block at all; it supplies segment revenue and segment operating income (E-01) and filing-computed margins, and it explicitly withholds segment capital. FACT [29] (E-01, seg.assets, status not_found): "We do not identify or report internally our assets (other than goodwill) or capital expenditures by segment, nor do we allocate gains and losses from equity method investments, interest, other non-operating income or expense items, or taxes to segments." would_change: if a ROIC series above a stated cost of capital existed for every period, the "returns persist … but share is not shown or has drifted" option would become available; if it showed ROIC below cost of capital in any period, the bottom option would come into range.

What the bundle does give on returns is a segment operating-margin record that moves in both directions. FACT [30] (E-01, seg.op_income, CNBU): "CNBU | $2,182 | $442 | $5,812 | $73", with filing-stated margins "CNBU | $2,182 | 43% | $1,919 | 42% | $442 | 17% | $5,812 | 41% | $73 | 1%". FACT [31] (E-01, seg.op_income, SBU): "SBU | (9) | 76 | 362 | (631)". FACT [32] (E-01, seg.op_income, MBU): "MBU | 217 | 301 | 604 | (395)". FACT [33] (E-01, seg.op_income, EBU): "EBU | 98 | 124 | 112 | 133". FACT [34] (mu-20250529, Risk Factors): "In the past five years, annual percentage changes in DRAM average selling prices have ranged from plus low-teen percentage range to a minus high-40% range. In the past five years, annual percentage changes in NAND average selling prices have ranged from plus low-30% to a minus low-50% range." FACT [35] (mu-20250529, Revenue by Business Unit): "SBU revenue increased 7% for the third quarter of 2025 as compared to the third quarter of 2024 primarily due to increases in bit shipments, partially offset by declines in average selling prices for NAND." INFERENCE [36, from 30–35]: within the four periods disclosed, two of four segments swing from nine-month operating losses to profits (SBU, MBU) and one swings from profit to a quarterly loss (SBU, $(9)m in Q3 2025 against $76m a year earlier), which is a record of price-cycle sensitivity rather than of persistence.

(c) Pricing defence, directly. FACT [37] (mu-20250529, Results of Operations): "Sales of DRAM products increased 15% primarily due to an over 20% increase in bit shipments, partially offset by a low-single-digit percent range decrease in average selling prices"; "Sales of NAND products increased 16% primarily due to a mid-20% range increase in bit shipments, partially offset by a high-single-digit percent range decrease in average selling prices." FACT [38] (mu-20250529, Results of Operations, Q3'25 vs Q3'24): "Sales of DRAM products increased 51% primarily due to a mid-20% range increase in average selling prices"; "Sales of NAND products increased 4% … partially offset by a low-20% range decrease in average selling prices." INFERENCE [39, from 37–38]: on the bundle's own periods, DRAM price realisation rose year over year while both DRAM and NAND prices fell sequentially — price is moving with the cycle in both directions, which is the definition of an inconclusive pricing-defence test rather than evidence of either a defended or a broken price.

STEP 3 — SELECTION. INFERENCE [40, from 6, 11, 18, 23, 28, 29, 36, 39]: named mechanisms are described in the filings (brands and capitalised process technology; proprietary process-driven per-bit cost reduction), the share test is unresolvable because no share figure for Micron or any leader appears in the bundle, and the return-persistence test is unavailable because no ROIC series or cost of capital is supplied — which is exactly "a mechanism is described … and the outcome tests are inconclusive on the bundle's periods". The two higher options are unavailable on their own terms: the top option requires stable share among the leaders and ROIC above cost of capital in every period (neither is in the bundle, and the cx.capacity items that gate it carry no quantity, per [19]–[21]); the "returns persist above the cost of capital" option requires a persistence result I cannot obtain from [29]. The bottom option is also unavailable: mechanisms are evidenced per [1]–[4] and [14]–[15], and segment operating income is positive in aggregate in all four disclosed columns except the nine months ended May 30, 2024 ("$2,490 | $941 | $6,891 | $(797)", mu-20250529 segment table), so "no mechanism is evidenced and returns do not persist" is contradicted. "The filings do not support any assessment" is too strong: [30]–[38] support an assessment of pricing and segment profitability, they just do not settle it.

ASSUMPTION: none supplied beyond the bundle; in particular I have not assumed any industry bit-share figure, any peer cost-per-bit, or any cost-of-capital value.

DURATION — what follows. INFERENCE [41, from 22, 34, 36]: if capacity additions by the named incumbents arrive without commensurate demand, the disclosed ASP swing ranges in [34] and the segment record in [36] imply segment returns can reverse within one to two quarters, so nothing in this bundle supports a durability claim beyond the four periods it covers; the coming segment recast (E-01, seg.basis_note: "we will report financial results under this new structure starting with our 2025 Annual Report on Form 10-K") will also break comparability of the only outcome series the bundle contains.", "what_would_move_it_down": "If, over the next four quarters, aggregate segment operating income turns negative again while the filings attribute it to average selling prices falling below cost — as in the nine months ended May 30, 2024, when total segment operating income was $(797)m with SBU at $(631)m and MBU at $(395)m — then returns would be shown not to persist alongside mechanisms that are only described, and the bottom option ("the moat is a story about a moat") would become the supported one."}
